text: Exclusive All Stories Exclusive: 91trucks lays off nearly 100 employees, shuts stores as growth slows 91trucks co-founder and chief executive officer Siddharth Sharma confirmed that the company has reduced its headcount, without confirming the exact numbers. Harsh Upadhyay 22 Jun 2026 10:43 IST Follow Us New Update Commercial vehicle marketplace startup 91trucks has carried out a major restructuring exercise that resulted in the departure of nearly 100 employees and the closure of several stores, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter. As per Entrackr's sources, around 100 employees have left the company over the past few weeks, leaving the startup with a team of roughly 50 people. Based on the current and former headcount, the exits account for nearly 70% of the workforce. Responding to Entrackr’s queries, 91trucks co-founder and CEO Siddharth Sharma confirmed that the company has reduced its headcount and said, “The restructuring only impacted approximately 30% of our workforce. We are still over 200 strong.” “As a business model, it was a conscious decision to move out of a few markets, primarily in South and Central India, though this only impacts 20% of our store network today,” he added. "The company was doing well, but growth projections made earlier could not be achieved over the last six months," said a person aware of the development, who requested anonymity. Several sources attributed the slowdown to macroeconomic challenges and weaker demand across the commercial vehicle segment. "Demand has softened due to macroeconomic conditions and ongoing geopolitical tensions. Business has not grown at the pace that was expected," said another source. However, some people familiar with the company's operations said conditions vary across markets. "The reality in smaller towns is different. Transport operators and truck owners continue to face challenges related to diesel and petrol prices, which has affected vehicle purchase decisions," one source said. According to sources, the company has also scaled down its offline retail presence. Nearly two dozen 91trucks stores have been shut over the past few months, with most closures concentrated in southern India and MP. Entrackr spoke with more than half a dozen store operators associated with the network. They independently confirmed the closures on the condition of anonymity. “As we continue organizing this highly fragmented market through trust, transparency, and ease of doing business, we have undertaken certain strategic and structural changes. After careful evaluation, we decided to focus our efforts on strengthening our presence in the North Indian market—which is substantial—while exiting a few geographies. This decision was driven primarily by the operational complexities and timelines involved in backend processes, particularly RC transfers and related compliance activities,” said Siddharth Sharma. He added that the company will focus on strengthening its presence in northern India, expand teams in line with growth plans, and pursue strategic partnerships to support its commercial vehicle ecosystem. The restructuring has also affected senior leadership. Sources told Entrackr that the company's country head has exited the organisation recently. Entrackr could not independently verify the circumstances surrounding the departure. The development comes three months after 91trucks acquired Motorfloor and Trucksfloor, two mobility-focused platforms operated by Bhubaneswar-based Indiyanet. The acquisition was aimed at strengthening the company's presence in the commercial vehicle ecosystem. According to another source, the company also held discussions to raise around $10 million in fresh funding. However, the proposed round did not close. Siddharth Sharma did not comment on the fundraising talks. Founded by Siddharth Sharma, Abhishek Gautam, and Vikas Sharma , 91trucks operates a platform focused on commercial vehicle discovery, financing and related services. In May 2025, the company raised around $5 million in a Series A round led by Arkam Ventures, with participation from Titan Capital, Sparrow Capital and Atrium Angels. The round valued the company at approximately $33 million. The developments come at a time when several startups in the automotive retail, mobility and commercial vehicle ecosystem are grappling with muted demand and a tougher funding environment. Industry executives and investors tracking the sector said that startups that expanded aggressively through offline networks could face further consolidation, workforce reductions and business shutdowns if capital remains difficult to raise and demand recovery stays slow.
